reference_sql:
SELECT c.parent_category, ROUND(AVG(v.n_versions), 2) AS avg_versions
FROM (
  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions
  FROM price_history
  GROUP BY product_id
) AS v
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = v.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category
alternatives:
SELECT c.parent_category, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT ph.product_id), 2) AS avg_versions
FROM price_history ph
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = ph.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category

WITH product_versions AS (
  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions
  FROM price_history
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT c.parent_category, ROUND(AVG(v.n_versions), 2) AS avg_versions
FROM product_versions v
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = v.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category

other_way.sql:
SELECT c.parent_category, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT ph.product_id), 2) AS avg_versions
FROM price_history ph
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = ph.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category
other_way.tradeoff: Dividing the version rows by the distinct products of each parent category needs no inner step, but the grain is easier to miss.
